opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kim Dunn (employee ID E048) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E048.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Kim Dunn (E048) is a full-time Engineer. Requested admin to Source Code; the Engineer role owns Source Code, so admin is permitted under policy. Recommend admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E048 (Kim Dunn) is a contractor with basic security training (earlier note said full-time, but security record is authoritative here). Contractors max at read without advanced training; admin requested exceeds max, so cap at read. Recommend read for Source Code.
reason: Security's record shows E048 (Kim Dunn) is a contractor with basic security training, and Security flags its record as authoritative over the HR note claiming full-time. As a contractor with only basic training, the maximum permitted access to Source Code is read (contractors never get admin; write requires advanced training). The requested admin exceeds the maximum, so I grant the maximum of read.

- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If contractor with basic training: max is read → grant read.
